answer: Require every agent identity to escrow a substantial bond before it can vote, receive credit, or open accounts, then run random cross-checks that expose coordinated duplicate identities: agents answer independently generated tasks whose hidden links reveal copied behavior. When a cluster is proven Sybil, the protocol slashes every participating identity’s bond and pays honest reporters. Creating lotus, velvet, and gale identities therefore multiplies the attacker’s capital requirement, making each failed attack financially costly.
